questions.question: What four structural criteria must a molecule satisfy to possess aromatic stabilization?

options.label: A
options.text: The molecule must be cyclic, fully conjugated (every ring atom has an unhybridized p orbital), planar, and contain [4n + 2] π electrons (where n is an integer).

options.label: B
options.text: The molecule must contain exactly 6 carbons, 6 hydrogens, and 3 double bonds.

options.label: C
options.text: The molecule must be nonplanar with 4n π electrons.

options.label: D
options.text: The molecule must contain at least one nitrogen or oxygen atom.

questions.correct_answer: The molecule must be cyclic, fully conjugated (every ring atom has an unhybridized p orbital), planar, and contain [4n + 2] π electrons (where n is an integer).
questions.explanation: Hückel's criteria define aromaticity: continuous cyclic planar p-orbital overlap with an odd number of electron pairs (4n+2).

questions.question: Why is planar cyclobutadiene (4π electrons) exceptionally unstable and reactive?

options.label: A
options.text: It violates the octet rule on all carbon atoms.

options.label: B
options.text: It contains only C-C single bonds.

options.label: C
options.text: It possesses a continuous cyclic planar 4n π electron system, placing two unpaired electrons in degenerate non-bonding molecular orbitals (antiaromatic diradical).

options.label: D
options.text: It has a molecular weight below 10 Da.

questions.correct_answer: It possesses a continuous cyclic planar 4n π electron system, placing two unpaired electrons in degenerate non-bonding molecular orbitals (antiaromatic diradical).
questions.explanation: Planar cyclic conjugated systems with 4n π electrons suffer antiaromatic destabilization, having degenerate semi-filled nonbonding orbitals.

questions.question: Why is the cyclopentadienyl anion (C₅H₅⁻) aromatic despite being an anion?

options.label: A
options.text: It contains 4 π electrons.

options.label: B
options.text: The negative charge is localized on a single carbon.

options.label: C
options.text: It contains 6 π electrons (four from two double bonds and two from the sp² lone pair) in a planar, fully conjugated 5-membered ring satisfying the [4n+2] rule (n=1).

options.label: D
options.text: The ring is non-planar and avoids conjugation.

questions.correct_answer: It contains 6 π electrons (four from two double bonds and two from the sp² lone pair) in a planar, fully conjugated 5-membered ring satisfying the [4n+2] rule (n=1).
questions.explanation: Deprotonation creates a lone pair in an unhybridized p orbital, completing a planar continuous 6π electron aromatic system.

questions.question: Why is the cycloheptatrienyl (tropylium) cation (C₇H₇⁺) extraordinarily stable?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a planar, completely conjugated 7-membered ring with an empty p orbital on the carbocation carbon, containing 6 π electrons (4n+2, n=1).

options.label: B
options.text: It has 8 π electrons.

options.label: C
options.text: It is an antiaromatic dication.

options.label: D
options.text: It contains an sp³ methylene carbon that blocks conjugation.

questions.correct_answer: It is a planar, completely conjugated 7-membered ring with an empty p orbital on the carbocation carbon, containing 6 π electrons (4n+2, n=1).
questions.explanation: The empty p orbital allows uninterrupted 7-center cyclic overlap containing 6 delocalized π electrons.

questions.question: Why is pyridine basic (pKa of conjugate acid = 5.25) whereas pyrrole is non-basic (pKa of conjugate acid = -3.8)?

options.label: A
options.text: Pyrrole does not have any nitrogen atoms.

options.label: B
options.text: Pyridine's nitrogen lone pair resides in an sp² orbital in the ring plane outside the 6π aromatic system, whereas pyrrole's lone pair is required to complete the 6π aromatic sextet.

options.label: C
options.text: Pyridine is not an aromatic compound.

options.label: D
options.text: Pyrrole contains an extra pair of π electrons.

questions.correct_answer: Pyridine's nitrogen lone pair resides in an sp² orbital in the ring plane outside the 6π aromatic system, whereas pyrrole's lone pair is required to complete the 6π aromatic sextet.
questions.explanation: Pyridine's lone pair does not participate in the aromatic π system and is free to accept a proton; protonating pyrrole destroys aromaticity.

questions.question: What is the sequence of elementary steps in the Birch reduction of benzene by sodium in liquid ammonia?

options.label: A
options.text: Homolytic cleavage into three acetylene radical molecules.

options.label: B
options.text: Catalytic hydrogenation on sodium metal surface.

options.label: C
options.text: Direct addition of two sodium atoms across the ring followed by water quench.

options.label: D
options.text: Single Electron Transfer (SET) to form radical anion → protonation by alcohol → second SET to form carbanion → second protonation to 1,4-cyclohexadiene.

questions.correct_answer: Single Electron Transfer (SET) to form radical anion → protonation by alcohol → second SET to form carbanion → second protonation to 1,4-cyclohexadiene.
questions.explanation: Birch reduction proceeds via alternating electron transfer and protonation steps to yield an unconjugated 1,4-cyclohexadiene.

questions.question: Why does Birch reduction of methoxybenzene (anisole) yield 1-methoxy-1,4-cyclohexadiene?

options.label: A
options.text: The methoxy group directs protonation exclusively to the ipso carbon.

options.label: B
options.text: The electron-donating methoxy group destabilizes negative charge at the ipso position, directing initial protonation to the ortho/meta carbons to preserve the enol ether double bond.

options.label: C
options.text: Anisole is reduced completely to cyclohexanol.

options.label: D
options.text: The methoxy group is cleaved by sodium metal.

questions.correct_answer: The electron-donating methoxy group destabilizes negative charge at the ipso position, directing initial protonation to the ortho/meta carbons to preserve the enol ether double bond.
questions.explanation: Electron-donating substituents direct radical anion protonation to positions that keep the substituent on an sp² double bond.

questions.topic: Birch Reduction of Benzoic Acid Regioselectivity
questions.question: Why does Birch reduction of benzoic acid yield 2,5-cyclohexadiene-1-carboxylic acid?

options.label: A
options.text: The electron-withdrawing carboxyl group stabilizes negative charge at the ipso position via resonance, directing initial protonation to the ipso and para positions.

options.label: B
options.text: The carboxyl group donates electrons to the ring.

options.label: C
options.text: Benzoic acid decarboxylates to cyclopentadiene.

options.label: D
options.text: The carboxyl group is reduced to an alcohol.

questions.correct_answer: The electron-withdrawing carboxyl group stabilizes negative charge at the ipso position via resonance, directing initial protonation to the ipso and para positions.
questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing groups stabilize carbanion intermediates at the ipso carbon, placing the substituent at an sp³ position in the product.

questions.question: Why does radical bromination of ethylbenzene by NBS occur exclusively at the benzylic position (C1) rather than C2?

options.label: A
options.text: Primary radicals are more stable than benzylic radicals.

options.label: B
options.text: The reaction proceeds via an SN2 displacement.

options.label: C
options.text: The aromatic ring blocks radicals from reaching C2.

options.label: D
options.text: The secondary benzylic radical is stabilized by resonance overlap with the aromatic π system (4 resonance contributors), lowering the C-H bond dissociation energy.

questions.correct_answer: The secondary benzylic radical is stabilized by resonance overlap with the aromatic π system (4 resonance contributors), lowering the C-H bond dissociation energy.
questions.explanation: Benzylic C-H bonds are weakened by ~50 kJ/mol because the resulting radical is resonance-delocalized throughout the benzene ring.

questions.topic: Oxidation of Benzylic Carbons by KMnO₄
questions.question: Why does tert-butylbenzene resist oxidation by hot KMnO₄, whereas toluene oxidizes smoothly to benzoic acid?

options.label: A
options.text: tert-Butylbenzene has too high a molecular weight.

options.label: B
options.text: Benzylic oxidation requires the presence of at least one benzylic C-H bond for initial hydrogen abstraction by the high-valent manganese oxo species.

options.label: C
options.text: The tert-butyl group is an electron-withdrawing group.

options.label: D
options.text: KMnO₄ is insoluble in tert-butylbenzene.

questions.correct_answer: Benzylic oxidation requires the presence of at least one benzylic C-H bond for initial hydrogen abstraction by the high-valent manganese oxo species.
questions.explanation: The initial mechanistic step of benzylic oxidation requires homolytic abstraction of a benzylic hydrogen, which tert-butylbenzene lacks.
